reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents OneCoin as a money-making opportunity through projected coin-value increases, paid packages, token quantities, and future earning benefits. It describes participation through buying packages or splits, receiving tokens, later selling or trading them, and earning through direct sales, matching bonuses, and generation-based network compensation. A prediction disclaimer is included, and completed transactions, realized returns, token liquidity, and reward delivery remain unverified.

opening.argument: Judge, the price discussion should be read as a conditional forecast, not a promise of returns. The speaker expressly calls the figures projections and acknowledges that the price can fall or produce no profit. He also says that reaching the charted values depends on members' efforts. Those qualifications matter when deciding whether the video guarantees a financial outcome: its optimistic scenario is presented as a possibility, not an assured result.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening identifies priced packages, tokens, and a statement about selling coins. Those establish what the speaker proposes, but not that the projected coin price or any individual's return is guaranteed. The speaker explicitly qualifies the projection as uncertain. The judge should distinguish an aggressive financial pitch from a claim that its forecast is certain.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The disclaimer limits the price forecast; it does not change the offer being made. The speaker introduces mining as a way to make money, describes paid packages and tokens, and says coins can be sold for cash. The case does not depend on proving a guaranteed price or a completed return. It rests on the video's invitation to pay into a mining-and-token earning arrangement.

opening.argument: Judge, much of this presentation is instructional. The speaker explains cryptocurrency in terms of cryptography, supply, and demand, then walks through tokens and splits. He tells viewers they can sign up for free to examine background material and documents before deciding what to do. That supports reading the video as an explanation of how the proposed system operates, rather than treating every description of a possible earning path as proof of deceptive solicitation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening treats the explanation of packages, tokens, and selling as solicitation. But explaining those steps is also necessary to teach viewers how the proposed system works. The speaker specifically directs them to review background materials, including audit and compliance documents. The cited statements do not establish that anyone actually bought a package, received a return, or was denied the chance to evaluate the offer.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The educational material leads into an explicit money-making pitch. The speaker says he will show viewers how to make money with OneCoin, gives paid package prices, explains earning through mining and team building, and ends by asking whether viewers want to mine coins now. An invitation to inspect documents does not turn that purchase-and-earn presentation into a neutral tutorial.

opening.argument: Judge, the priced offerings are also described as education packages: the speaker says the education level varies with the package. He describes a free sign-up option for examining background material, rather than a demand for an immediate payment. The presentation certainly discusses tokens and bonuses, but the cited material does not show a completed purchase, a failed withdrawal, or a guaranteed return. On this record, the package prices alone do not establish that the underlying transaction is deceptive.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening points to paid packages, tokens, future sales, and network compensation. Those are real parts of the presentation, but the speaker also identifies education as a package component. Nor does saying a coin may later be sold establish that a particular sale or return occurred. A compensation plan can be examined critically without assuming that the package has no ordinary service component.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the packages educational does not remove their earning mechanism. The presentation connects money to tokens, splits, mining, and coins, while the speaker says mining and team building are ways to make money. He also describes commissions from direct sales and later generations. A completed loss is unnecessary to recognize that the video promotes paid participation for anticipated mining and recruitment income.
